mass_kg.note: the Russian article's table gives the basic R-27 253 kg without naming its seeker; the R-27T taken as it, its own mass not given

length_m.note: the table's 3,795 mm for the basic R-27, not tied to a seeker; the English article's R-27R is 4.08 m, so the shorter is taken as the infrared R-27T's

power_up_s.note: no source gives a missile's power-up or power-down time: 1 s for every missile, an engineering assumption so a strike waits for its missiles as a real one does

power_down_s.note: no source gives a missile's power-up or power-down time: 1 s for every missile, an engineering assumption so a strike waits for its missiles as a real one does

explosive_kg.note: a game reference: War Thunder's su_r_27er (the R-27ER's) (TGAF-5); no manufacturer or encyclopedia gives the charge

gurney_kms.note: TGAF-5 (TNT/RDX/aluminium, Russian) is not in Cooper's table: as HBX, its nearest composition - an estimate

drag_area_m2.note: the isolated store's CD S below Mach 0.8 at a Reynolds number of 1e7 per metre, built up from its design (hangar storedrag.py: Hoerner's body of revolution 0.00513, its base 0.00220, its fins' friction 0.00629 m^2): an estimate by one method for every store

munk_volume_m3.note: its body's unstable moment across a flow, q x this x sin(2 x angle) (Munk, NACA Report 184): its volume 0.1502 m^3 from its design, times Lamb's k2 - k1 = 0.977 for its fineness 16.4 (hangar storedrag.py): an estimate by one method for every store

side_slope_m2.note: its fins' and base's force across it per radian of crossflow, over the dynamic pressure (hangar storedrag.py: one fin pair's Helmbold slope carried onto the body, slender-body theory's base): an estimate by one method for every store

side_arm_m.note: where that force acts, behind the store's CG (hangar storedrag.py: its fins' quarter chords, its base)
